fieldData.short-verdict: The Regent Phu Quoc blends modern minimalist design with Southeast Asian charm — a truly aspirational resort, in a not-so-aspirational location.
fieldData.recommended-for:
• Couples and design-minded travelers
  • IHG elites with lounge access (huge Regent Club value)
  • Anyone happy to stay on-property and let the resort be the destination
fieldData.not-recommended-for:
• Travelers wanting a vibrant destination beyond the gates
  • Anyone unwilling to make the long trip to Phu Quoc
  • Those who prioritize local dining and sightseeing over on-property luxury
fieldData.cash-points-value-notes: The nightly cash rates for this property range from 300-600 dollars a night for the lowest tier room. Incredible value for what you get. Points required range from 0.5-0.8 CPP, which isn't great, but the cash rate is so good it is carried on value.
fieldData.opening-thoughts:
I had heard nothing but good things about this property leading up to this stay. I was so excited to stay here that I made it the first stop on my minimoon — and boy did that pay off. I say this as the highest level of compliment: walking through this resort felt like walking onto the set of The White Lotus. This resort is modern and beautiful and still manages to preserve its regional inspiration.

We knew this resort would be beautiful, and the level of service matched what was already an amazing property on paper. I think it's pretty clear by now — we absolutely loved this resort.
fieldData.room-layout-review:
This might be a little unfair, because we booked a king suite, actually received an ocean view suite, and then paid up to get what might have been the most beautiful room on site: the King Terrace Villa. The room is perfection, just pure perfection. I challenge you to find a single spot in it that feels out of place or even boring. The room is littered with tasteful custom design elements throughout, yet feels spacious and clean. The size is much larger than you would expect — ours was roughly 165 sq m, way more space than we even knew what to do with. It is all top-notch, custom-made, with high-grade finishes. The fridge and drawers are filled with silverware, platters, or food that's refilled every day and completely complimentary. As standard, there is a coffee maker and a tea set in the kitchen.

From the door to the bedroom there's a clear path, with the living room set off to the side but easily accessible at any point. There's an easy path to the pool as well, with floor-to-ceiling windows letting in plenty of natural light and a beautiful view of the outside greenery. We had two garden-view suites below us and while they weren't occupied, I do think the soundproofing would have been fantastic either way.
fieldData.bathroom-review:
Once again, pure perfection. I could just stare at this bathroom for ages, it's just beautiful. Double vanities on opposite sides of the bathroom give each partner their own space. Showers were beautiful and worked well, with no issues with drainage or hot water. The bathtub is huge (it can definitely fit two people) and they even provide a little headrest so you can put your head back and relax while you bathe. The toilet has an automatic bidet, and soundproofing was excellent.

My only gripes were that the headrest smelled a little used, and that the bathroom door was made of glass — by design, but it did not give me the privacy I want when I use the bathroom. Custom-made robes and slippers are provided for both guests and the personalization is phenomenal: they gave me a pair of larger men's slippers while my plus one received smaller slippers made for women. Lighting is also fantastic, with an option for bright or mood lighting. I preferred the mood lighting, since it accentuated the natural spa-like character of the bathroom.
fieldData.bed-sleep-review:
No issues here. The sheets were super comfortable and gave us a great night's sleep. The duvet kept us warm without overheating — a rare combo. They also had a choice of pillows, a standard at luxury hotels; we stuck with the standard ones provided. There is also the option of blackout curtains or light-leakage curtains. I personally prefer light leakage since it helps me wake up early, though my plus one preferred blackout. It was nice to have both readily available at the touch of a button.

With this room I would say there are no real hallways, as the hallway only leads to our room. The other hallways outside lead to the two suites underneath, and there would never be foot traffic we could hear because of the layout. Temperature and humidity are very well controlled, considering Vietnam gets incredibly humid — especially when we went, during the rainy season.
fieldData.tech-implementation-review: Great integrations, with the curtains and blackout curtains tied to easy-to-find buttons. Lights are almost all hooked up to a master switch. There are USB chargers but no USB-C chargers, which unfortunately warrants a slight demerit in my book. Good entertainment in place: the TVs, while I didn't use them much, seemed to have an okay selection of channels. The Wi-Fi was perfect, no troubles with speed — my plus one even had a video meeting and connected flawlessly despite the other party being on the other side of the world. The keys are keyless, and I don't remember if there's app integration, but I think there's probably the option.
fieldData.amenities-review:
There is no shortage of pools, spas, saunas, beach access, or anything else you would need at this resort. If I'm not mistaken there are over 200 pools, which seems absurd until you're on property and realize that pretty much everywhere you look there's a pool — maybe two, maybe three. They're beautiful, mostly infinity pools or shallow tide pools you can dip your feet in if you just want the feeling of water at any time. The gym was probably one of the most beautiful I've ever seen: all the equipment you'd need, ellipticals and treadmills, and it even provided coconut water along with energy drinks and other snacks.

Above all else the star of the show, at least for us, was the Lounge, which we had access to because of my IHG Diamond membership (a tier selection bonus). It was probably one of the most beautiful rooms in the whole hotel — and that says something. The staff were as good as you can ask for, and the food was some of the best I've ever had, probably the best I'll ever have in a lounge. We opted out of the provided breakfast to eat at the lounge as much as we could. And did I mention the all-day champagne? Not just any champagne — we looked the bottle up and each one was worth upwards of $90-$100. Insane value. If you don't have status you can pay for daily entrance at $150 per person per day; it sounds like a lot, but considering they serve dishes featuring wagyu, truffles, and caviar, it may not be the worst deal. I've definitely paid more for less at all-inclusives.

We don't have kids, but we took a look at the kids' facility and I have to say, I wish I were a kid visiting this hotel. It was large, sprawling, and had everything you could ask for: gyms, swings, playgrounds, and even modern entertainment like video games.
fieldData.atmosphere-design-review: The design philosophy is clear throughout, and the sense of place on Phu Quoc island could not be any better. This place really makes you feel like you are in Vietnam — just the luxurious side of Vietnam. There's natural lighting everywhere you go, and the artificial lighting sets a mood of serenity throughout the resort. There are speakers everywhere, even in places you don't expect, like back hallways where you'll hear tranquil music playing. The design is consistent and you clearly know what region you're in. Everywhere you look there's the regional symbol — and not just that, there's the resort's own Phu Quoc motif, which I thought was very neat, littered throughout the whole property and even in our bathroom. It's even in the chocolate bars.
fieldData.maintenance-upkeep-review: While the resort is not brand new, the maintenance and upkeep is fantastic. I'm particularly sensitive to signs of aging in furniture, unclean hallways, and scuffs, and honestly I didn't notice any. One of the elevators was down during our stay and there were times when pools were closed when they maybe shouldn't have been — I might attribute that to it being the wet season. It was very, very windy when we first arrived, so I think it was more of a safety thing. Pretty much everywhere you go there's someone cleaning and picking up leaves, not just on the road but under the shrubs as well, where you normally wouldn't notice unless you looked very closely. That really goes to show the attention to detail involved.
fieldData.location-and-or-view-review:
If this hotel were in Hawaii, it would go for $1,500-2,000 a night — it's that good. But of course it is not in Hawaii, and that becomes painfully clear when you decide to go exploring. This hotel is almost singlehandedly brought down by the inescapable reality that Phu Quoc is just not a great destination. I'm sorry, it's true. The beach the Regent sits on is beautiful, I agree, and the views from just about anywhere in the hotel are beautiful too. It manages to offer seclusion from the rest of the island.

But what is it surrounded by? Empty, near-abandoned buildings whose pastel pink and blue colors are nothing but eyesores. Then take a trip to nearby Sunset Town, a short 20-25 minute taxi away. It's the closest thing I can find to the dystopian feel of 2010s China (where I lived for a decade). The town was quite clearly built unnaturally and gives off an eerie vibe of inauthenticity, stemming from the fact that they built the infrastructure before the demand. No one is living in these buildings. It feels like a declining amusement park, where only the shop is open but the rest of the building is dark, empty, and lifeless.
fieldData.check-in-arrival-review:
The check-in experience was as good as anywhere I've ever been. From the minute you arrive, a chauffeur takes your luggage and you won't think about it again until you get to your room, where it has already arrived and been set very neatly just past the door. Your "butler," whom you've been in contact with before arriving, greets you warmly as you step out of the car and shows you to either the lobby or, in our case, the lounge, where we were offered refreshments and even food while check-in was completed away from us.

The room was ready when we arrived, but they wanted us to see the other rooms available, even for a paid upgrade. We're happy we did, because we chose the King Terrace Villa for a small upgrade of about $250 a night and it was well worth it — one of the greatest rooms we've ever stayed in. When we got to the room, our luggage was neatly set near the entrance and they took the time to explain everything in detail: where the thermostat was, how to control the blinds and lights, which kitchen appliances were available. We truly felt welcome. The whole check-in experience was easy, warm, efficient, and just fantastic.
fieldData.service-operational-excellence-review:
Of everything we'd seen up to this point — the stunning rooms, the flawless design philosophy, the feeling of place — none of it had my plus one and me gushing more than the level of service we experienced at this facility. Perhaps it was because we went during the off-season, where the staff-to-guest ratio is more manageable, but whatever it was, I'm here for it. We went to the Park Hyatt Saigon just after this resort — a property well known for its service, where the best concierges from across Vietnam travel to train — and it didn't come anywhere close to the level of service we found at the Regent Phu Quoc.

If a worker saw you, they would immediately drop what they were doing to smile and wave. Every staff member was professional, warm, remembered your name, and had a sense of anticipation, knowing almost exactly what you'd want at all times. Every department was consistent. They were very responsive — you'd get WhatsApp access directly to the concierge and could text them whenever you wanted anything. They didn't always respond instantly, but almost always within 30 minutes to an hour, and when they did, they fulfilled the request as soon as they could. Housekeeping came twice a day and was honestly amazing: they'd rearrange and clean top to bottom, leave small chocolates each time, and bundle up any electronic cords.

The staff seemed genuinely happy to work there and had nothing but good things to say about IHG and the system they work in. Some of our best service came at the lounge, where we were greeted every day — someone would come to open the doors whenever they saw us approaching from a distance. As for champagne, any time you got close to finishing your glass, someone would come by to refill it without you even having to ask. The concierge was genuinely useful: they helped us book a show in Sunset Town, gave good advice on taxis and what to do, and helped us exchange money before we set off. I had my sights set on the luxury yacht/catamaran and told a concierge I wanted to book it as soon as I arrived. He actually advised against it given the season and weather (overcast, windy) — I didn't listen, booked it anyway, and he was right; it wasn't the greatest experience and was very expensive. Props to him for trying to steer me away. I'd love to give service a perfect score, but there were a few moments — occasionally at breakfast they weren't the most responsive, and at certain facilities some staff were just trying to get their job done — where there was a little room to improve.
fieldData.service-peak-anticipation-review: Most of my sentiment on the service is in the previous section, but this hotel really does its best to go over the top to make sure you have a great time. Any time we had a request, I knew I could speak to any staff member, who would either immediately seek to fulfil it or direct me to the most appropriate person. Their use of WhatsApp for direct communication has the potential to be a dud, but in this case it gave us on-demand access to their exceptional service.
fieldData.operational-excellence-review:
Operations here are perfection. There are staff everywhere, trained to do every little thing to ensure the guest experience is perfect — from picking fallen leaves out of the shrubbery, to trimming each and every bush and tree, to running nets through the ponds to keep their surfaces clear and serene. Walking through the grounds is almost a spectacle in how they keep operations so smooth at the scale they run.

They also give us access to a WhatsApp line where we can reach them directly for one-off requests. I'm not sure who takes the texts, since it seems to change daily, but they respond and execute tasks anywhere from 5 to 30 minutes. Altogether, I am still in awe of how they keep operations so tight. Kudos to whoever trains the staff.
fieldData.housekeeping-review: Housekeeping here is the best I've experienced and as good as it can possibly get. They came around twice a day, made the bed, and cleaned the pool and poolside area each time. Towels were replaced and all shoes were placed in the proper location. Beyond perfectly maintaining the room, they took the time to organize our luggage off to the side, neatly place our shoes at the entrance, and even tie up all of our electrical cables. The room was spotless every time we came back, and they timed their visits for when they knew we were away, keeping their footprint as unnoticeable as possible.
fieldData.breakfast-review:
I'm only talking about the breakfast complimentary to everyone here (not the lounge breakfast), but this is one of those times where the food looked better than it tasted. When we first arrived, I was blown away by the design, the plethora of food options, and the incredibly fresh presentation of each cooking island. Food was prepared on the spot, with certain stations cooking to order, and there was also an à la carte menu. Unfortunately the à la carte wasn't very good — my plus one and I each ordered a dish the first day and another the next, and after that we pretty much stuck to the buffet.

Coffee was excellent, with a large selection ranging from coconut coffee to Vietnamese coffee and of course regular Americanos. Service was good, sometimes a little slow, and there was always a pretty large crowd whenever we went. Variety is the biggest strength here: a bakery section, fresh fruits and smoothies, cold cuts, and a well-stocked kids' section. The main warm food section is split between Western, Chinese, Korean, and Vietnamese options. My favorite dishes came from the Korean and Chinese sections, and the pho was honestly pretty good — not comparable to the best places in Ho Chi Minh, but solid in its own right.
fieldData.crowding-exclusivity-review: We went during the off-season, so crowd management was very easy on their end. The hotel wasn't booked to max capacity and the employee-to-guest ratio was very good at the time. We never had to wait for breakfast and the lounge was always available to us. The only gripe we had was that some of the activities filled up quite fast — there were only 8 to 10 spots per activity and somehow they were all booked out before we were able to go.
fieldData.departure-experience-review: Great checkout experience, no complaints here. The bill was presented to us with all the charges explained. Luggage was picked up from our room and delivered directly to the taxi that came for us. The farewell was warm and late checkout was granted, though our flight was at 2pm so we didn't fully take advantage of it. While we waited for our taxi, they graciously handed us refreshments — it was very hot, so that was definitely appreciated.
fieldData.final-verdict:
Needless to say, I absolutely loved my four nights at this hotel. From top to bottom, the best hotel or resort stay I have had, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking to visit Phu Quoc or even Vietnam — especially if you have lounge access.

Some might look at the score and say, hey, if this was the best stay ever, why didn't it get a 95 or even 100? That comes down to the location and exceptionally minor gripes. Still, if you have the chance and are travelling through Vietnam, this hotel is worth the detour.

fieldData.short-verdict: A decent value option in the center of downtown Denver. You get what you pay for here.
fieldData.recommended-for:
• Business travelers who need a central downtown Denver base
  • Value-first guests who care more about price than polish
fieldData.not-recommended-for:
• Travelers or tourists looking for luxury experience
  • Globalists looking for elite recognition
  • Anyone who values a spa or pool during their hotel stay
fieldData.opening-thoughts: I probably shouldn't even review this hotel, since it feels more like a work hotel than anything, but I stayed there and I have a few thoughts, so here I am. This will be a shorter review because there isn't much to say.
fieldData.room-layout-review: The rooms are kind of funny. They clearly had a design in mind, but the execution is just not there. I can't explain why, but the room just felt uncanny — like it has all the properties of a nice room, but the material and the build quality just did not follow through. Maybe it was the insulation, or the color of the paint, but something just didn't feel right.
fieldData.bathroom-review: The bathrooms are a little better than the room itself. Really though, nothing great. I'm pretty sure the bathrooms at Hyatt Place are better.
fieldData.bed-sleep-review: The sleep actually wasn't great. There was humidity leakage from the outside and the bedding was average at best. I didn't hear much noise from the hallway or outside.
fieldData.tech-implementation-review: There's Wi-Fi and USB connections. At least they don't charge their loyalty members for Wi-Fi.
fieldData.amenities-review: There's a gym here. No spa or pool. I guess it could be worse.
fieldData.atmosphere-design-review: At least they tried to make it different and give it a little design flair. The lobby isn't great though — it's barely a lobby. There isn't much public space anywhere, and the finishes just aren't good enough to really matter.
fieldData.maintenance-upkeep-review: My room wasn't dirty, but the upkeep clearly wasn't their primary concern. Most of the room is dated and worn.
fieldData.location-and-or-view-review: It's in the center of Denver, which I guess is the whole point of a Hyatt Centric hotel. It really serves its purpose as a location-based work hotel and very little more.
fieldData.check-in-arrival-review: Check-in is pretty much what you would expect from an extended stay hotel. They check you in, give you your keys, and nothing else. There is an optional valet service you can pay to use.
fieldData.service-operational-excellence-review: Staff at check-in and at breakfast were friendly and helpful. That was my main interaction with staff outside of the valet.
fieldData.service-peak-anticipation-review: Nothing above and beyond the basics. Pretty much what you would expect from an extended stay hotel.
fieldData.operational-excellence-review: Nothing wrong with operations here. My Globalist benefits were recognized without issue. Elevators worked, billing was fine, and overall everything worked. I guess there isn't much for them to fault on.
fieldData.housekeeping-review: Housekeeping came by once and fulfilled the basics, like making the bed and refilling the towels and toiletries.
fieldData.breakfast-review: Breakfast here is surprisingly good. It was definitely the highlight of the stay. The potatoes were some of the most delicious hotel breakfast potatoes I have ever had. They are generous with what they give you, offering an à la carte selection, coffee and juice.
fieldData.crowding-exclusivity-review: Not overly crowded, but easily accessible to everyone, including anyone walking in off the street. There is limited security here for a city hotel.
fieldData.departure-experience-review: The departure here is similar to an extended stay hotel. You check out, bring your own bags down, and put your bags into the car. The bill was accurate at least, and the departure team was warm and friendly.

fieldData.short-verdict: A slightly dated but still luxurious Park Hyatt in a wonderful location — a top-tier option for anyone staying in Busan.
fieldData.recommended-for:
• Travelers who value an excellent location and view
  • Hyatt Globalists looking for elite status recognition
  • Anyone looking to pair a luxury base with the Haeungdae nightlife
fieldData.not-recommended-for:
• Guests who need a brand-new hard product
  • Anyone booking without status, where the upgrade and spa perks disappear
  • Travelers assigned an interior-facing room
fieldData.opening-thoughts:
We had been staying in a city nearby (my wife's hometown) and decided to stop over in Busan for a short trip — the perfect opportunity to stay at the (sometimes) maligned Park Hyatt Busan. It's a Park Hyatt after all; how bad can it be? Well, I'm happy to report that while the property has its flaws, it was still a nice stay and I can definitely recommend it to those staying in Busan. After all, you don't have many other luxury options for elite benefits.

My mother and father-in-law stayed at the Signiel nearby, while my wife, my brother-in-law, my sister-in-law and I took two rooms at the Park Hyatt Busan. I used a Guest of Honor award for their room and tried my luck on an upgrade purely on my Globalist status.
fieldData.room-layout-review:
We were given the Ocean View Family Suite, and when we entered, my wife and I both agreed the view was fantastic — a sprawling panoramic view of the Gwangan Bridge from the bedroom. Wake up and just admire it. The room makes good use of the space available: there's a good path from the door to the bedroom, with the living room and the bathrooms on the way. There wasn't much wasted space, and most of the walls had some kind of decoration or art. They really tried to incorporate the feeling of being in Korea, and specifically Busan, with some traditional art pieces.

There is no shortage of natural lighting, and I personally enjoy the dark ambient artificial lighting at night. The walls felt pretty well soundproofed — I didn't hear anyone in the hallways. Storage was abundant, with a wardrobe and hangers for coats or shirts. Finish quality was high, though some pieces felt a bit tired, like the furniture.

My only real complaint is that parts of the room felt a little strange. There are pillars with mirrors covering each side, presumably to make the space feel bigger and to reflect the gorgeous view. They did get in the way at times, making it hard to move through the living room or even get out of bed. That said, I do think the room was the highlight of my stay.
fieldData.bathroom-review: I really like the bathrooms at the Park Hyatt Busan. While they didn't have a complete spa vibe, they did feel very comfortable, modern, and clean. The bidets are modern and automatic, and most of the material is marble. Drainage from the showers was very good, and I really liked the bath — it reminded me of the baths I would take in the onsens in Hakone. Robes, slippers, and toiletries are all on point, and ventilation after a hot shower was very good. Absolutely no problems with water pressure or temperature.
fieldData.bed-sleep-review: The beds felt very comfortable. My wife and I both had a relaxing, recharging sleep. The blackout curtains and the light curtains worked very well and were automatic. I didn't hear the HVAC at all, and there were no hallway or neighboring noises to wake me up at night. Temperature and humidity in the room were solid, if not perfect.
fieldData.tech-implementation-review: Absolutely no problems with the tech implementation in this room. Wi-Fi was fast and available to high-tier members. There were USB and USB-C charging outlets, placed at both sides of the bed — very convenient locations. There was automation for the lighting and the curtains, and it could be controlled mostly from the bed. A nice little Park Hyatt touch I appreciate is that there's almost always a TV visible from the bath, so if you want to watch your favorite show while relaxing in the tub, you can.
fieldData.amenities-review: I thought the pool was really pretty here. The gym was pretty well stocked, and the spa was complimentary to Hyatt Globalist members but $40 entrance otherwise. There was a lounge of sorts, but really it was more like a bar. Overall, what it had was pretty good, but there wasn't anything over the top that would make you say "wow."
fieldData.atmosphere-design-review:
To get to the lobby you have to take one or two elevators, depending on where you're coming from. From the parking lot that's two elevators, and it can be pretty confusing your first time up. From the front entrance it's one elevator and slightly less confusing. The materials used in the lobby and public spaces were very beautiful — either granite or marble, and the cut of the stone gave a feeling of luxury and elegance.

I've read some reviews of the property where people disliked the lighting, feeling it was too dark. I personally enjoyed it; I think the darkness gives a sense of elevated luxury, though at times it was too dark to see where you were going — an unintended feature, I'm sure. While I didn't feel the public spaces incorporated much Korean or Busan design philosophy, the general design is consistent throughout the hotel and with many other Park Hyatts. As far as I can tell there wasn't a signature scent or music, though I did see them selling a signature scent; I wasn't sure whether they just weren't pumping it that day or it was too subtle for me to smell.
fieldData.maintenance-upkeep-review: Overall there was pretty good upkeep in the hotel. I didn't notice any obvious scratches or scuffs. The furniture is a little old and dated — that might just be the design of the furniture itself, but I wasn't the biggest fan. The bathroom had high-quality finishes throughout and felt like a true high-end hotel. Housekeeping did a good job as well, and I didn't particularly notice any uncleaned or unmanaged areas.
fieldData.location-and-or-view-review: If you're staying in Busan, this is a prime spot. You could argue that being on Haeundae Beach is a better location, but you'd be sacrificing the panoramic view of the Gwangan Bridge, which I thought was one of the highlights of the stay. Either way, it was only a 10 to 15 minute walk to Haeundae Beach, so not too bad.
fieldData.check-in-arrival-review:
Check-in here was probably the worst part of this hotel, and it really got us off to a bad start. From the parking lot it was hard to figure out where we needed to go. We took the wrong elevator the first time, going to the fourth floor instead of the proper check-in on the thirtieth. What's strange is that there was a separate check-in desk on the fourth floor and I don't know its exact purpose — the fourth floor does contain the gym, sauna, and spa, so maybe it was check-in for those. Either way, they seemed to notice we were lost, holding six pieces of luggage, and didn't bother directing us to the right place.

We had to go all the way back to the first floor, figure out the right elevators, and take those up to the thirtieth. From there the process was pretty good — a standard check-in, with a front desk clerk who was nice and helpful and accommodated our request for an early breakfast delivered to the door. They didn't assist us with our luggage to the room, which is usually standard at a high-end hotel.
fieldData.service-operational-excellence-review: I don't have anything bad to say about the service — it just wasn't particularly outstanding. Everyone was generally nice, but they didn't go out of their way to help us. The one thing they did really well: we needed to leave the hotel by 4:30am and couldn't make breakfast, so we asked for an early breakfast delivered to our room, which they happily organized. It arrived at 4:30 sharp, packaged very nicely and ready to take to the airport. That really saved the service score.
fieldData.service-peak-anticipation-review: There was nothing here that was over-the-top good in terms of service, but I did appreciate that when we told them we had to leave very early in the morning, they accommodated us by leaving a fully packed breakfast by our doorstep at exactly the time we asked. Very impressive.
fieldData.operational-excellence-review: Generally done pretty well. We didn't notice any huge operational flaws besides what happened on arrival. Elevators were all in service and decently fast, given they have to run up and down thirty floors. We didn't have a chance to experience housekeeping since we left after one night.
fieldData.housekeeping-review: Unfortunately we were unable to fully experience the housekeeping, so this score is incomplete — but the room was very clean when we entered.
fieldData.breakfast-review: We were unable to experience the full breakfast spread since we had to leave before 6am, but we did receive a packed breakfast to-go at our doorstep. The packed food was very neatly presented and consisted of pastries and fruit. My brother-in-law took a picture of the actual buffet breakfast and had good things to say about it, though neither he nor my sister-in-law raved about it.
fieldData.crowding-exclusivity-review: The hotel wasn't crowded, though there were bottlenecks at times, namely at the elevators due to the peculiar design. The pool was also quite popular, which I noticed every time I walked by even though I never used it myself. The lobby could be busy at times, but luckily the top-floor lounge and restaurants had seating available pretty much always.
fieldData.departure-experience-review: Easy checkout experience. We were not offered help with our luggage, unfortunately, which was a shame since it was already so difficult to exit the premises — let alone with four large suitcases.
fieldData.final-verdict:
I think this Park Hyatt is underrated and definitely a good option for any Hyatt Globalist who can get the ocean view suite. My brother- and sister-in-law had the interior-facing family suite, and while I actually enjoyed that room configuration more, the view was basically a look into the office building across the street. Not my idea of luxury.

The hotel is very close to Haeundae Beach and opens you up to the nightlife Busan has to offer. I enjoyed the hotel more than my rating suggests and wouldn't hesitate to return should I visit Busan again.

fieldData.short-verdict: A luxurious, classically themed hotel with beautiful art and intentional design, renowned in Ho Chi Minh City for its exceptional service.
fieldData.recommended-for:
• Tourists wanting a central location to multiple points of interest
  • Globalists looking for elite perks while traveling
  • Guets who value classical, historical design and artwork
fieldData.not-recommended-for: • Travelers who prefer contemporary design and luxuries
fieldData.opening-thoughts:
Coming off our trip to the Regent in Phu Quoc, we decided to spend another three days in Ho Chi Minh City, and naturally we chose the Park Hyatt Saigon. This is a hotel I'd heard a lot about on other travel sites and had been looking forward to for a very long time — exceptional things about the service, the design, and the overall feel of the hotel. It has a reputation as the best hotel in Ho Chi Minh City.

The price was very reasonable for someone coming from America, but compared to other stays in Ho Chi Minh it was a fair bit more expensive. I was happy to pay the premium as a Hyatt Globalist, knowing I'd get a hefty upgrade along with free breakfast — something else I'd been looking forward to, as this is considered one of the best breakfast spreads in the Hyatt portfolio. I was delighted to hear we'd been upgraded to the Park Executive Suite instead of the Park Suite I originally expected — a pleasant surprise, as this was the second-highest tier of suite on property.
fieldData.room-layout-review:
We were originally assigned the Lam Son Suite, a regular suite overlooking Lam Son Square. On arrival we were upgraded to the Park Executive Suite, which I was very excited about. I'd seen pictures already and was expecting a classical feel, with a layout inspired by early-to-mid 1900s upper-class accommodation. The room itself was huge and nicely decorated, but part of me — and unfortunately my wife as well — didn't feel it was the greatest use of the space. There were swaths of empty space that weren't filled with art or anything noteworthy to look at. The furniture, beautiful in its own right, did invoke the feeling of being in an antique or vintage shop, which may be something some people really enjoy.

I won't give the decoration the "dated" label, because I really don't think it is. My main gripe is that the room felt large but barren, which left a slightly uneasy feeling. To be honest this may have just come down to the specific room we were in. When we were leaving, the front desk graciously allowed us to stay past our late checkout in one of their standard rooms — and this surprised me, because I actually preferred the standard room to the executive suite despite it being less than half the size. There was far less empty space to look at and more of a feeling of intentional design. I still appreciated the generous upgrade, but I think the executive suite could use a refresh.
fieldData.bathroom-review: The bathrooms are beautiful in their own right. I'm used to more modern amenities like a modernized toilet with an integrated bidet; here the bidet was off to the side, something you don't typically see these days and something I didn't even want to use, since it felt messy to move from the toilet onto the bidet. Otherwise, robes and slippers were provided, as is the norm at a Park Hyatt. Lighting was decent throughout. There wasn't mood lighting and it didn't feel like a spa — just an upscale older-century bathroom. No problems at all with water temperature or pressure.
fieldData.bed-sleep-review:
Almost everything here was good. The mattress was comfortable, the linens were high quality, and there were decent pillow options. With the curtains and blinds closed there's almost no light leakage. I will say that noise leakage from the hallway is a problem at times — we could hear children running down the hallway, which wasn't an issue at night but does ruin the feeling of exclusivity a little.

My biggest gripe with sleep quality, and something I had to fix myself, is the humidity and temperature control. The minute you walk into the room the humidity is noticeable. I was very uncomfortable for the first hour or two, so much so that I called the front desk and requested a dehumidifier. When your hotel is somewhere like Ho Chi Minh City, well known for being humid and tropical, you'd want built-in humidity control. They provided one dehumidifier for two large rooms, and I had to place it in the middle myself so it would cover both the living room and where we slept — arguably the more important of the two. I give them props for having a dehumidifier, but these things need to be built into the hotel or provided ahead of time. The thermostat was clearly quite old; you needed a fingernail to properly adjust the temperature on the touchscreen, which was probably several years, if not over a decade, old.
fieldData.tech-implementation-review: Really decent tech implementation. Wi-Fi was pretty good and there were outlets in every location you'd want. There were some light and smart controls, but the lighting and curtains were all manual — not a problem, since housekeeping came by every evening to close the blinds. Entertainment systems were modern and the TVs were huge. There was a USB charger but no USB-C outlets.
fieldData.amenities-review:
The pool was central, beautiful, and hidden behind a garden in the courtyard. We tried to get some close-up photos but were stopped by staff requesting we not take professional photos of the pool. I thought that was fine — it preserves a sense of exclusivity for patrons who just want to swim. The gym was large and had most of what you need, a little old-style with some tired equipment, but generally pretty good. The spa looked beautiful from the outside, though I didn't get a chance to use it; there are endless massage parlors throughout the streets of Ho Chi Minh City charging a fraction of the on-site price, but if you want that high-end feeling you're better off with the hotel spa.

One activity we did do was the art tour, at a modest $20 per person. This might have been the highlight of the stay. The guide was knowledgeable, patient, and very personable, and having her explain the art gave us context on what this hotel is about, its history, and even the history of Ho Chi Minh City and Vietnam. My wife and I both came to appreciate the hotel a lot more after the tour, and I highly recommend it even if you don't particularly enjoy art.
fieldData.atmosphere-design-review:
The lobby and public spaces are the highlights of this hotel. The lobby is beautiful, with fresh flowers, and the artwork is grand and makes an instant statement the minute you walk in. Everything felt really high-end and intentional, with beautiful finishes throughout, on the walls and even the ceilings. The lounge just off the lobby is open to the public, serves afternoon tea, and is beautifully designed with three large chandeliers overhead — we took the afternoon tea service one day just to sit and appreciate the room.

There is a clear design philosophy running through the whole hotel and into the artwork. The hotel really draws on the roots of Vietnam's history and is a celebration of the city and country. The lighting is clean, with tons of natural light flooding in from every angle. Music in the lobby is a nice touch, though I wasn't able to discern a signature scent.
fieldData.maintenance-upkeep-review: The hotel is very well maintained and clean. It opened in 2005, making it over 21 years old, with updates in 2014, 2015, and 2019 that keep it fresh and lively while maintaining its classical French colonial style. This property is probably much older than any I have reviewed in the past, yet it manages to use that longevity to add to its charm. On the walls, and specifically in the art collection, you can see that the owner has curated many spectacular pieces over the years, with a clear evolution in stylistic preferences.
fieldData.location-and-or-view-review: The hotel sits on Lam Son Square in District 1 of Ho Chi Minh City — the heart of the city, with the iconic Opera House just steps away and tourist destinations like Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica and the Central Post Office a short walk away. While the hotel is in the center of a chaotic city, it truly shines in that its immediate vicinity is calm and walkable, as if it were the calm eye of a chaotic storm.
fieldData.check-in-arrival-review: Fantastic check-in that checks all the boxes. We were helped with our luggage on arrival and ushered to the desk, where we were offered a delicious arrival beverage. The check-in agent was extremely friendly and helpful, offering recommendations for nearby sights and places to eat. After we received our room key, another attendant led us to our room and explained the turndown service and the automated lights.
fieldData.service-operational-excellence-review: Service was quite fantastic and consistent, with the only hiccup at breakfast — and I think that came down to the fact that the hotel was packed. I wouldn't have been surprised if they were near full capacity. Even at the earliest breakfast times the dining area was nearly full, and most of the breakfast staff appeared stressed. There were pretty long lags between being seated and being served, which surprised me given how many good things I'd heard about breakfast service here. Otherwise, most of the staff were extremely friendly and willing to help, and all were highly proficient in English.
fieldData.service-peak-anticipation-review: Many of the staff were willing to go above and beyond to ensure a great experience, with two moments as the highlights. The first was the art tour, where our guide was simply fantastic. The second was at checkout: when we mentioned our flight was close to midnight, they went out of their way to move us into another room after the 4pm late checkout, letting us stay from roughly 4pm to 9pm until we called our Uber. Seriously, I don't know any other hotel that would do something so gracious.
fieldData.operational-excellence-review: Operations were generally well done. We didn't notice many hiccups during our few days here — the only one being that the checkout staff didn't know the check-in agent had offered us a room past checkout. Not a big deal, since they cleared it up, but a lapse in continuity of communication. Otherwise the elevators worked well and we never had a long wait. Pools and restaurants operated efficiently despite the high occupancy, though I wish the servers had been less stressed. We requested a dehumidifier for our room and it arrived within 15 to 30 minutes, which was great.
fieldData.housekeeping-review: Housekeeping here is excellent, as expected of a Park Hyatt. The initial service is comprehensive, covering the room, bed and bathroom while also tidying cables and shoes. Turndown service is offered as well, including closing the shades and refilling the ice bucket. A great touch all around — I couldn't ask for much else.
fieldData.breakfast-review:
The breakfast is so good, so fresh, and so high quality. They offer a wide assortment of pastries and breads, espresso actually made from an espresso machine, fresh fruit, and an à la carte menu that's a dream, including items like banh mi and homemade pho. However, I was surprised — if not shocked — that I did not find the croissants very good. For a French colonial-themed hotel of this level, that is unacceptable.

Back to the à la carte items: I found them all very tasty, but compared to the same dishes I could find out in the city, I didn't want to waste precious stomach space on the hotel version. If this breakfast were anywhere other than Ho Chi Minh City, I might have rated it higher.
fieldData.crowding-exclusivity-review: This hotel is packed — well, the lobby is packed, so the whole hotel felt packed. When I'm returning from a day out in hot, humid Vietnam, I just want to get to my room as soon as humanly possible, take a shower and decompress. I do not want to wade through a sea of people on my way in. A lot of Vietnam's upper class like to spend their afternoons in the lounge here, which makes it feel much busier than it is.
fieldData.departure-experience-review: Excellent departure. Our bags were handled by the bellman, and we were given late checkout even beyond the standard Globalist late checkout. Billing was accurate, and the staff showing us out were warm yet professional.
fieldData.final-verdict:
I think my rating of the hotel oversells how much I personally enjoyed it. It has a lot of good aspects and screams personality, but maybe the style just didn't suit me. I really expected a lot coming in and, I hate to say it, it didn't live up to the hype for me.

Still, I can recommend this stay — it's fantastic for the price, and there seem to be generous upgrades offered as long as there is availability.
fieldData.meta-title: Park Hyatt Saigon Review: Classical Luxury in District 1
fieldData.meta-description: Our 82/100 review of the Park Hyatt Saigon: French colonial design, a standout art tour and generous Globalist upgrades, with service that trails the hype.
fieldData.name: Park Hyatt Saigon

fieldData.short-verdict: Centrally and conveniently located in the heart of Porto, this InterContinental somehow shows its age despite a recent renovation.
fieldData.recommended-for:
• Sightseers who want the most central address in Porto, beside São Bento station
  • IHG Diamonds who can put a suite upgrade award to work
  • Travelers happy to eat breakfast out in a great food city
fieldData.not-recommended-for:
• Guests who want resort amenities — there is no pool, spa or lounge
  • Anyone expecting a recent renovation to read as new
  • Travelers who need a quiet room away from street-level construction
fieldData.opening-thoughts:
This was a property I'd heard a lot about and I was very excited to finally stay here. It makes many top-10 InterContinental lists for its classical European architecture, central location, and historically significant building. It was also recently renovated, with an overhaul to most of the rooms and suites. Porto is one of my favorite cities in the world, so needless to say I'd been looking forward to this stay for quite a while.

Upon entering, I immediately felt a sense of — I don't even know how to say it — that feeling that something was just off. We were welcomed by the doormen, who helped us with our luggage, a nice touch, but the lobby didn't feel like it had the attention to detail I'm used to at a luxury five-star stay. There was too much paneling in the design and not enough decoration to truly create a vibe. Check-in was in the main atrium, just next to the stairs and chandelier, which, though pretty, honestly looked better in pictures. The lobby was also infested with a gaggle of horse flies — not their fault, but they should have taken measures to prevent something like that from ruining the guest experience. The rooms themselves were well renovated and did exude a touch of the luxury I didn't feel in the lobby, but they were already showing signs of wear and tear.
fieldData.room-layout-review:
The room we received was the one-bedroom suite, and it was a very awkward design. There's a tiny patio outside that isn't really a balcony and isn't really a backyard either. There's no view to the outside, just a wall covered by fake plants. There's a chair and table out there, but they might as well not be, because there isn't enough room to sit comfortably. The layout of the room itself is awkward and doesn't offer enough space to navigate or place your luggage.

The rooms here benefit from having just been renovated and I hate to knock them, but I'm kind of surprised by what they did. The build quality is good but not great — they used good materials, but not ones you'd see at truly top-end hotels. I'm being harsh, but only because I actually like the InterContinental brand and hate to see corners cut at a property with the potential to be one of their flagships.
fieldData.bathroom-review: At least the bathrooms are nice. This might have one of my favorite hotel showers, since it offers both the overhead rainfall and the side nozzles, which can run at the same time — something I dream of owning in a future home. The layout is otherwise nice, with a clear view out to the tiny patio. There's plenty of space for two people at the vanity, and the toilet is situated in a decent location with plenty of privacy.
fieldData.bed-sleep-review: The mattress, linens and pillows were comfortable, as expected of an InterContinental, but not exceptional. There is a pillow menu available on request. There was limited hallway noise interrupting our sleep, as the bedroom had the living room and bathroom insulating us from the front door. I will say that humidity in Porto isn't a huge issue generally, but that room managed to hold onto it, and that's something I'm quite sensitive to. Temperature control was great and responsive — no complaints from me there.
fieldData.tech-implementation-review: The renovation might have added some automation, which does elevate the stay. There are controls for the lights but not the curtains, and the outlets handled universal plugs and USB, but no USB-C.
fieldData.amenities-review: I'll be a bit harsh with this one — the hotel really doesn't offer amenities. I can understand not having a pool; this is a repurposed historic building, so adding one just isn't viable and may even be unnecessary. What I can't excuse is the lack of a lounge. There is space; I just think they chose not to build one. Lounges are money sinks with little upside for the hotel if people are willing to book anyway. I did enjoy the food in Porto very much and it wasn't expensive to eat out, but come on — you're an InterContinental. There's an expectation of a lounge. Other than that, the gym is decent but not spectacular.
fieldData.atmosphere-design-review:
The design philosophy is consistent throughout and invokes a European old-money vibe — or at least what I imagine that to be. There's a healthy balance of artificial and natural lighting throughout. No signature scent, which was disappointing; we stayed at the InterContinental Parnas and they had a signature scent we liked so much we bought a bottle to take home. In the rooms there's a wonderful integration of modern and old-school design.

That said, it looks better in pictures. There's a feeling of datedness and a lack of upkeep the second you walk into the building — the kind of thing that can be photoshopped out of curated images but won't go unnoticed if you visit. The overall design of the lobby is ornate, if not borderline tacky, though I personally enjoyed it since it felt European and exotic to me. Parts of the lobby felt barren and lacking in intentional design. There's a hallway offshooting from the entrance used just for shops and jewelry displays, with no active customers, and it gave the feeling of being abandoned. Finishes are seemingly high-end, with plenty of marble throughout, but I couldn't shake a feeling of cheapness. The bar and lounge looked modern and beautifully designed, so I'll give them that.
fieldData.maintenance-upkeep-review: I don't feel like the hotel is maintained at an adequate standard. It was recently renovated, yet it does not exude any sense of having just been refreshed.
fieldData.location-and-or-view-review:
The location honestly can't get any better than this — right in the heart of Porto, next to São Bento train station. A lot of the time we would wander from one point of interest to the next and walk past our hotel several times a day completely naturally. I won't penalize the hotel twice for our lack of a view; I'm sure it's fantastic in other rooms.

There was also construction during our stay, which I assume will go on for a few more years. That isn't something I can fault the hotel for, but it does make the location slightly more inconvenient than it should be, and there's the noise of construction coming from the square. Again, not their fault, but it does affect the experience if you stay while it's ongoing — which it probably will be for the next three to four years.
fieldData.check-in-arrival-review: Could use work. We did have assistance with our luggage, though the bellman lacked warmth and I felt uncomfortable handing it over — like I was inconveniencing him by asking for help. I did appreciate that our upgrade was handled well in advance and we knew the exact room we'd be getting days ahead. At the counter, the person assisting us was clearly in training and had no idea what the loyalty tiers were; the manager swooped in whenever she got stuck, and the rest of check-in went smoothly. When we got to our room, our welcome amenity wasn't ready, despite the room having been assigned to us days in advance. Not the worst thing, but it does make an impression.
fieldData.service-operational-excellence-review: We found the staff generally warm, friendly and helpful. The highlights were the breakfast staff and the manager who assisted us at check-in — all consummate professionals, while maintaining the warmth that makes you feel they don't detest their job or their guests.
fieldData.service-peak-anticipation-review: Service really peaks at breakfast. They have an excellent staff-to-guest ratio there, and there were always different servers looking to clear our table or help us order more à la carte items, coffee or juice. The bellboys were also helpful on arrival, and the concierge was a good resource. They never really go above and beyond otherwise, though, so don't expect too much.
fieldData.operational-excellence-review: Operations ran fairly smoothly over our four days. Elevators ran well, though I don't think there were that many floors anyway. No real problems that we noticed, which is a good sign.
fieldData.housekeeping-review: Housekeeping is only once a day, but they do the basics well — making the bed, cleaning the room and replacing toiletries. Nothing above and beyond that we noticed, but we never had any issues.
fieldData.breakfast-review:
Breakfast here — honestly, don't waste your stomach space. There's so much delicious food in Porto that there's no need to eat what they provide. The buffet has limited hot options but does offer a wide array of pastries, juices, fruit, cold cuts and cheeses. The cold offerings were honestly above average, but I really need to start my day with freshly made food.

The pre-prepared hot foods were generally unappetizing to look at, let alone eat, and believe it or not the à la carte options are worse. We couldn't make it past one or two bites of each thing we ordered à la carte, and we stopped ordering entirely after the first two days. It felt like they lacked a proper head chef — simple dishes were botched and seasoning just wasn't there. Cafeteria food, anyone?
fieldData.crowding-exclusivity-review: I actually enjoyed the capacity at this hotel. It wasn't empty enough to feel deserted, but it also wasn't so crowded that I felt claustrophobic or neglected. The entrance has heavy foot traffic, but it doesn't spill into the hotel itself.
fieldData.departure-experience-review: Solid departure. At checkout the staff were friendly and we were helped with our luggage to our taxi. Billing was accurate as well.
fieldData.final-verdict:
My experience was still overall positive despite my complaints. I had a really good time in Porto for four nights, and the location of this hotel really made that happen. The room is still nice overall, and while I had problems with the breakfast, not eating a big breakfast did leave me more room to enjoy the wonderful food Porto has to offer.

There also aren't many high-end large-chain hotels in Porto, surprisingly enough. The Yeatman opened recently and looks fantastic, but I've learned the grass isn't always greener.

fieldData.meta-description: Our 68.5/100 review of the InterContinental Porto - Palacio das Cardosas: the most central address in Porto, but a renovation that already shows its age.
fieldData.name: InterContinental Porto

fieldData.short-verdict: A dated hotel in a not-so-central location — not my first choice for anyone deciding to stay in Lisbon, even with lounge access.
fieldData.recommended-for:
• Business travelers whose office is nearby
  • Guests who simply need an IHG stay in Lisbon on points
  • Anyone indifferent to lounge quality and breakfast
fieldData.not-recommended-for:
• Tourists, who face a 15-20 minute trek to the nearest point of interest
  • IHG Diamonds expecting status to carry the stay
  • Anyone with other options in a city full of better-value hotels
fieldData.opening-thoughts:
After spending four nights in Porto, we had one night to stay over in Lisbon before our flight the next morning. I wanted to book an InterContinental because I wanted the lounge access and somewhere a little closer to the airport but still near enough to the city center to enjoy the sights.

I hate to say it, but after a night here I cannot wholeheartedly recommend this hotel. While most of the service was quite lovely, especially at the lounge, the hard product itself falls short in ways that shouldn't be representative of the InterContinental name — whatever that name means at this point.
fieldData.room-layout-review: The room is okay. InterContinentals have a particular style and don't tend to stray from it in most of their city hotels. We stayed in the most basic room, albeit with an upgraded view, and there was actually decent space for a standard room. The quality of the furniture wasn't bad.
fieldData.bathroom-review: This is your standard single-vanity InterContinental bathroom. Nothing inspirational, but functional nonetheless. Everything worked and the water pressure was great. Unlike the InterContinental in Porto, there were no showerheads aimed at the body. The materials used were standard but good quality.
fieldData.bed-sleep-review: I thought the sleep here was a bit better than at the InterContinental Porto. Similar bedding and linen, but the temperature and humidity control were better. There was limited noise at night from the hallway, and from outside since we were on a very high floor.
fieldData.tech-implementation-review: There are no automated controls for the lights and shades, which puts this behind newer, more recently built hotels with smart-room controls. The Wi-Fi is available and steady at least, and there are standard USB and outlet placements throughout the room.
fieldData.amenities-review:
There is a lounge (although it's not very good) and a well-equipped fitness center. Other than that, there really isn't anything else — no pool, no spa, and no programming or activities.

On the lounge: it's located at the back of the main lobby, behind glass doors. When we went it was staffed by one dedicated attendant, but as far as guests go it was basically empty — a bad sign. We arrived just in time for afternoon tea and were promptly seated and served. After trying the first pastry from the platter, we quickly realized why there were no other lounge members: the pastries were stale, tasteless or off-putting. We also had breakfast at the lounge, which was sparse, though whatever they did have tasted decent.
fieldData.atmosphere-design-review:
I really don't see enough effort here. This is as standard as an InterContinental gets. The only touch of flair is on the doors at the back of the lobby leading to the bar. The outside of the building is off-putting as well, and shows the age of the property before you put a single foot inside. I was pretty disappointed just pulling up and seeing the unkempt state of the walls and windows — to be fair, the building next door was home to the Four Seasons and looked equally dilapidated.

Inside, the lobby is uninspired and standard. The hallways lacked ambiance or a sense of place, and the rooms themselves were cookie-cutter too. Being inside the hotel, you'd have no idea you were in Lisbon.
fieldData.maintenance-upkeep-review: The hotel isn't dirty, but there are signs of aging everywhere. The walls are tired, the carpet is worn, the windows aren't clear, and most of the furniture looks like it has been there for decades. This hotel needs a refresh as soon as possible.
fieldData.location-and-or-view-review: The location might have been one of my least favorite aspects of this hotel. On the map it looks like it's in the city center, but when you're actually traveling around, it's at least 15 to 20 minutes from even the closest point of interest. Maybe it's a great location for business travelers, assuming there are corporate buildings nearby, but for a tourist I would skip this property on location alone.
fieldData.check-in-arrival-review: We were helped with our luggage and the bellboy was very friendly on entry. Our luggage was sent up and arrived shortly after we got to the room. Other than that, check-in was standard: we received a floor upgrade and were denied any further upgrade even after asking.
fieldData.service-operational-excellence-review: The staff were all friendly and professional. I was especially satisfied with the service in the lounge, where the team was extremely pleasant and helpful. I know I complained about the lounge itself, but that had nothing to do with the one or two staff members operating it. There was no language barrier either.
fieldData.service-peak-anticipation-review: The extra half point here comes from the bellboy and the lounge staff, both of whom were memorably friendly. Other than that, we didn't notice any specific personalization in service or anticipation of our needs. Most of the staff were friendly but weren't trained to go above and beyond.
fieldData.operational-excellence-review: We didn't notice any glaring flaws in operations during our stay, though we only stayed one night. We were given lounge access right away without issue, our room was ready when we arrived, and the elevators worked well (probably because there weren't many people there). We didn't request late checkout, and the hotel was surprisingly well staffed.
fieldData.housekeeping-review: I'll leave this as an average score, since most InterContinentals do a pretty good job with housekeeping and typically don't offer turndown service in my experience.
fieldData.breakfast-review: Breakfast for IHG Diamond members is served in the lounge, and it was bare bones and very low effort. They offered the typical items — fruit, yogurt, cereal, pastries, some cold cuts and cheese — but had few self-serve warm dishes. The à la carte items were average at best and the selection wasn't great. I left disappointed in the breakfast and the lounge overall.
fieldData.crowding-exclusivity-review: Not many people, but it was well staffed for the number they had. The hotel is fairly out of the way from the tourist spots, so there's minimal foot traffic outside. This was the least crowded lounge I have ever been to — which makes sense given the quality of the lounge itself.
fieldData.departure-experience-review: Good, solid departure experience. The staff helped us with our luggage from the lobby into our taxi and were friendly on our way out. Billing was accurate and checkout didn't take long.
fieldData.final-verdict: I'll be honest, I don't hate this hotel, but if you are in Lisbon I would highly recommend staying somewhere else. There are so many amazing hotels in that city for a fair price; you shouldn't waste your time or money here. Even if you have IHG Diamond and lounge access, neither gets you very far at this property.

fieldData.meta-description: Our 55.5/100 review of the InterContinental Lisbon: warm staff and a lounge that disappoints, in a location 15-20 minutes from anything worth seeing.

fieldData.short-verdict: Upscale, refined luxury that is fitting for a city that feels just as grandiose.
fieldData.recommended-for:
• Globalists, who see some of the best recognition in the portfolio
  • Travelers who want an Inner Stadt address on Am Hof, steps from the sights
  • Guests who come for the spa and pool, among the most stunning in any city hotel
fieldData.not-recommended-for:
• Repeat visitors who have already worked through Vienna's museums
  • Travelers needing US power outlets
  • Anyone wanting a relaxed resort pace over refined city opulence
fieldData.opening-thoughts:
This is one of only two Michelin Key hotels in the Park Hyatt portfolio, so needless to say I was very excited about this stay. It was my first time visiting Vienna — I could even say I travelled to Central Europe just to stay here, because I was that hyped for this hotel. It's one of a few Hyatts in the city and the only one above a Category 3.

Being a Category 7, I used a free night award for the first night and 70,000 points for the next two, applying a suite upgrade award. At check-in they combined the three nights into one stay and upgraded me on the first night to a Park Suite to match the rest of the stay. Does this hotel live up to the hype? In my opinion it does, and if you're in Vienna I can definitely recommend you check it out — assuming you have the points or cash to do so.
fieldData.room-layout-review:
We stayed in a Park Suite, having been upgraded from a base King Deluxe room using a suite upgrade award. I had high expectations given how luxurious and opulent the pictures were, and while the room was quite spectacular, I will say the pictures made it look a little grander than it was. One drawback was the ceilings: high, but not incredibly high. We stayed on the fifth floor, and I'd read beforehand that rooms on the first floor have exceptionally high ceilings compared with the rest of the hotel. Ours weren't low by any means, just not big enough to make the space feel bigger than it was.

That said, there was more than enough space for my wife and me, and the closet space was humongous — one of my favorite things about the layout. The bedroom was a decent size, with just enough walkway on either side of the bed that I didn't feel like I had to climb over it, though I wouldn't be able to stretch my legs out on the wall side. The TVs are hidden in the repurposed fireplaces, revealed by sliding a mirror panel upwards — a nice touch I enjoyed. All the finishes were high quality, blending plaster, wood, marble, mirrors and metal. I never felt like I was staring at empty, purposeless wall space either, a subtle thing that adds that premium "designed" feeling to a room.
fieldData.bathroom-review:
If you've stayed at a Park Hyatt before you'll be quite familiar with these bathrooms, as they're standard across most Park Hyatts — not that that's a bad thing. Our Park Suite had double vanities, a nice standing shower, and beautiful marble finishes throughout. The main standout is the marble paneling framing the area behind the bath, which is both beautiful and a signature of this hotel; if you've scrolled through their room galleries, you'll have seen it as the centerpiece.

My two knocks: the toilets don't have many of the modern amenities you'd expect, like an automatic bidet or heated seat — quite standard, and almost a bit flimsy-feeling compared with bathrooms at other luxury hotels (they did flush well, so no problems there). And the bathroom just didn't feel grand or spectacular in any way. It felt like a great bathroom fitting for a great hotel, and no more.
fieldData.bed-sleep-review: Park Hyatt hotels always carry quality linens, pillows and mattresses, and this was no exception — my sleep was excellent. I didn't hear any noise penetration through the walls, and our room sat at the far end from the doorway, insulated by two or three sets of doors, so hallway noise would have been very difficult to hear anyway. The blackout shades did their job wonderfully and were fully automatic, and the HVAC made very minimal noise. The only downside was that humidity control in the room was just a touch lacking — it felt a bit more humid than I personally prefer, with no way to control it besides turning up the AC to dry the room out.
fieldData.tech-implementation-review:
For me personally the tech implementation was perfect, because I always bring a universal adapter. Had I not, I would have been very annoyed that all the outlets only accept European plugs. I'm sure the hotel carries adapters for this scenario, but the outlets also lacked USB-C ports.

Aside from that, the wall controls for the room were perfect and had everything I could want and then some — lighting adjustable to many different levels, automatic curtains, and even options for night lights and reading lights. Keyless entry was flawless and the Wi-Fi was available and stable.
fieldData.amenities-review:
The pool and spa might be among the most stunning I've seen in a city hotel. Just look at it — it feels like swimming in a Roman bath fit for an emperor (I didn't swim, but I was there). I used the gym every day and it was well equipped compared with average, though it lacked heavier free weights and there was no barbell or Smith machine. I didn't ding it for that, since it isn't always expected, but it's something I wish it had; it did have plenty of treadmills, bikes and ellipticals.

There's also a "lounge" on property that I think is used for cigar smokers, since it reeked of smoke when we went to check it out. We didn't use the spa, but we looked around and it seemed to have most of what you'd expect, at high quality — the sauna and steam bath both looked well equipped and spacious.
fieldData.atmosphere-design-review:
One of the strongest aspects of the hotel. The atmosphere and design truly make you feel elegant and high-end, giving a sense of place in the best way possible. The building used to be home to the Austro-Hungarian Monarchy bank, built in 1915. The exterior is beautiful and immediately familiar, with the iconic Park Hyatt logo and font above the entrance. Upon entering, the lobby is understated but grand; perhaps the weakest area of design is the check-in area, which appears quite standard, if not a little boring.

Where the hotel really shines is the centerpiece of the building, the Bank Brasserie — formerly the cashiering hall — now the main breakfast location, also housing a restaurant and bar. The ceilings are magnificently high, the walls are finished with thick, high-quality marble panels, and the rest of the space is lined with decorations, sculptures and design elements that enhance the feeling without tipping into tacky. The restaurant is an open-kitchen concept and you can watch the cooks prepare each meal; the dishware and silverware are high quality as well. I've already touched on the pool, but it really does add a layer of awe, with perfect mood lighting throughout the pool and spa area and classical music pumped through the water for an extra touch of class. The sense of place this hotel invokes is world class, especially for a city hotel.

Despite all this, one area where the hotel falls short is its hallways, which is surprising since Park Hyatts tend to put a lot of effort into the experience on each floor. The hallways here really feel dated — the walls aren't decorated well, the carpets are old and worn, and the windows are dirty and unclear.
fieldData.maintenance-upkeep-review:
The hotel opened in June 2014, and while it's generally well maintained, it can be apparent at times that it's over 10 years old and hasn't gone through a refurbishment. For me this tends to be most obvious in the flooring, where areas of the hardwood just seem to have more give than freshly laid boards. Some of the finishes and decor also have a slightly time-worn appearance — not the fault of property management, just age showing.

I noticed the furniture in our room felt a bit worn too, with scuffs on the console and in the closet space. Cleanliness was generally very good, especially in the Bank Brasserie area, but I did notice dust left on the curtains in our room, and the windows are quite dirty on the outside (I know they're hard to clean, but still). I think they did a good job with what they control most — vacuuming and dusting — but some things may need a refresh in the near future.
fieldData.location-and-or-view-review:
The location is perfect, on Am Hof, right in the center of the Innere Stadt. For us it was right next to the main high-end shopping street and close to several sights we wanted to see, including the Imperial Treasury, the Sisi Museum, and the historical museum. The Innere Stadt also holds the majority of the beautiful architecture you associate with Vienna, so just walking around outside the hotel was a joy.

Am Hof sits slightly off the busy street where some of the other high-end hotels are located, so while this may add two or three minutes of walking, it also shields the hotel from most street noise and foot traffic, giving a more exclusive, isolated feel without actually being isolated. If you visit during the holidays, the Christmas market is also very close by, making this a prime location at that time of year.
fieldData.check-in-arrival-review:
Our check-in was a bit marred by a bad personal experience, so your mileage may vary. When we arrived there was one single bellboy, already occupied helping the family in front of us with their luggage — the problem being that he didn't bother to acknowledge us or let us know he'd assist. We carried our luggage inside and the concierge at the desk barely looked up or offered to help. I began the check-in process while my wife awkwardly waited by the entrance with our three large suitcases, while the concierge and bellboy stood around without offering a trolley or a hand.

I understand this may sound entitled, but at a high-quality hotel — especially one at the calibre of a Park Hyatt — luggage assistance is a baseline expectation at check-in. We can perfectly well move our own luggage at a Holiday Inn, but not at this type of property. It took me asking the check-in agent (who was wonderful, by the way — a special shout out to Freya) before someone bothered to help.

Aside from that fiasco, the check-in desk is very standard and a bit bland, with no welcome drink offered. The agents were all very pleasant and professional, though, especially the one who helped us; she went through the details of the hotel and gave us excellent recommendations for nearby restaurants.
fieldData.service-operational-excellence-review: Aside from that first impression with the bellboy, service at the property was very warm and professional. Staff were always friendly when they approached us, and we never felt like we were bothering them when we made requests. Service was especially great at breakfast, where the whole team was friendly and attentive, coming by constantly to help us order more coffee or clear the table.
fieldData.service-peak-anticipation-review: On the surface the service is more or less perfect, but I did feel it lacked in anticipating our needs or going the extra step to fulfil requests — things that would be done at an ultra-luxury resort. No one really remembered our names besides the person who checked us in (Freya).
fieldData.operational-excellence-review:
Operations were generally good, with a few hiccups. Most of the time it felt smooth: the room was ready almost immediately when we arrived, with the welcome amenity waiting for us. There was very little downtime for the elevator despite there being only one, and staffing levels were excellent throughout the hotel and at breakfast, where service was on point and there right when you needed it.

There were a few times we made requests to our room — an extra hair net, a toothbrush — where the request was never fulfilled or we needed to call twice. That was surprising, since they were very delightful over the phone in taking the request, but they never followed through.
fieldData.housekeeping-review: Housekeeping was excellent, coming around twice a day — once in the morning and once for turndown service. A trademark of Park Hyatt housekeeping is that they tie and organize your cords, which I particularly enjoy. Our shoes were placed into compartments to keep them organized and our bed was made excellently each time.
fieldData.breakfast-review:
The food at breakfast was outstanding, one of the best I've had at a hotel anywhere. The quality of each dish was very high and there seemed to be no expense spared in sourcing good ingredients. The standout for me was the truffle scrambled eggs, and most of the dishes we ordered were very tasty. All the pastries were excellent, and there was self-serve caviar as well (though the blinis were stale from sitting out). The orange juice was very fresh and most of the fruit was sweet and ripe.

Sparkling wine is served with breakfast, though we didn't partake since it was early in our trip and I wanted to save the drinking for when we got to Prague.
fieldData.crowding-exclusivity-review: The hotel was never crowded and the staff-to-guest ratio was excellent at most times. I'm sure it can get busy and stressful during the holidays and Christmas market season, but when I went in the summer it felt great. A good portion of the travellers seemed to be there for business. Although there is only one main elevator, it was never occupied and we could get to our room with ease.
fieldData.departure-experience-review: Departure was standard, easy and fast. Our bill was accurate, we were helped with our luggage, and we were offered assistance in calling transport to the train station for our next destination, Salzburg. We were offered late checkout as a Globalist, which I didn't need since our train was at 8am. We also took the time to thank Freya in person, since she was so lovely at check-in and made a great dinner recommendation on our first night.
fieldData.final-verdict:
Overall, a wonderful experience and a standard-setting hotel. It definitely delivers on the opulent vibe we expect from a Park Hyatt, and I'd say it deserves its two Michelin Keys.

If I were to return to Vienna, I wouldn't hesitate to stay at this beautiful property again — though I don't think I'll return to Vienna any time soon, since I don't think the city has much more to offer tourists once you've finished all the museums and historical sites.
